name: Family Money Dashboard
intro:
⚠️ BEFORE STEP 1 — check you are in a test copy. Look for the small “🧪 Test copy” mark on the screen. It means this app has never seen you, which is what the steps below expect. If it is missing and the app already shows your own information, you have opened your real app: go back to your list and tap this app's name again, rather than using a bookmark, your history, or an icon on your home screen.

The Family Money Dashboard gives a household three answers every month: what to spend, what to set aside for once-a-year bills, and how much comes from savings. You will look around an example family, fill in a missing yearly bill, answer the app's questions about unclear payments, see what is paid from each account, change a setting, check it remembers after a reload and with no internet, then start your own setup. All the money here is pretend.

steps.do: Look at the screen the app opens on.
steps.see: A card headed “Three answers, every month” with two buttons: “Set up ours” and “Show me an example family first”.
steps.tip: If a “What would you like to do?” start menu comes up instead, tap “This month” — that is the start menu, and it is right.

steps.do: Tap “Show me an example family first”.
steps.see: A yellow card says “👀 This is an example family, the Hendersons. Tap anything — it is pretend money.” Under the month name is a card headed “🧮 (last month) in three parts” with these rows: 1 · Spend each month, 2 · Save for later bills, Regular budget, Income $9,200, Left over, 3 · As needed this month.

steps.do: In that card, tap the “Income” row.
steps.see: A sheet says “Income: $9,200” and lists Pension $5,400 and Social Security $3,800. Tap “Close”.

steps.do: Tap the “2 · Save for later bills” row.
steps.see: A sheet headed “Bills once or twice a year”. The Travel card shows red words starting “Booked: Spring cruise ($3,900”. The “Home insurance (yearly)” card says “unknown” at the top right.

steps.do: In the “Home insurance (yearly)” card, type the number below into the “Yearly cost” box, then scroll down and tap “Save”.
steps.see: A message says “Saved.” The Home insurance card now says “$400 set aside” at the top right instead of “unknown”. Tap “Close” at the bottom.

steps.do: Scroll down to the card headed “🚩 Worth a look”.
steps.see: Among its lines is “Charged twice? RIVER GRILL, $86.40”, and at the bottom of the card a “Show … more” button.

steps.do: Scroll to the buttons near the bottom of the page and tap “❓ Getting to know you”.
steps.see: A sheet headed “Getting to know you · item 1 of …”. The card shows $120, the words “VENMO PAYMENT 1022”, and under the card “What was this?”.

steps.do: Tap “One-time purchase”.
steps.see: It moves on to item 2: $400, “ZELLE TO S MORGAN”, and asks “What was this?”.

steps.do: Tap “As-needed help for a person”, then tap “Nephew Sam”.
steps.see: Item 3: $1,200, “LAKEVIEW ACADEMY TUITION”. It asks “This looks like School costs paid by the 529 — right?” and the dark first button explains that a matching $1,200 came in from “COLLEGE SAV PLAN DISTRIBUTION”.

steps.do: Tap that dark first button. On the next item ($64.20, TOYSRUS ONLINE) tap “Not sure — skip for now”.
steps.see: Now $1,450, “MOUNTAIN ROOFING CO”, asking “This looks like Mountain cabin · Repairs & upkeep — right?”.

steps.do: Tap the dark first button. On the next item ($850, CHECK 1047) tap “Done for now” at the bottom.
steps.see: The sheet closes and you are back on the main screen.

steps.do: Tap “📋 Lists”, then tap “🤝 Nephew Sam · loan”.
steps.see: The list says “2 lines, $1,000 in all — a loan, to be paid back.” with $400 and $600 lines and a running total. Tap “Back”: the Lists sheet also shows “🎓 Paid by the 529” with $1,200 and “❔ Not sure yet (1)”. Tap “Close”.

steps.do: Tap “🔗 What’s paid from where”.
steps.see: A sheet with a card for “🏦 Joint checking ••4410” listing the bills that come out of it, starting with LAKESIDE MORTGAGE SERVICING $2,150.

steps.do: In the Joint checking card, tap “This account is closing”. Then tick the first box in the list.
steps.see: The sheet is headed “Moving everything off Joint checking ••4410”. After the tick, the line at the top changes from “0 of … moved” to “1 of … moved”, and the ticked line says “moved” with today’s date. Tap “Back”, then “Close”.

steps.do: Tap the card headed “🏡 Our household”.
steps.see: A sheet with three parts: “⏰ Coming due”, “🗝️ Where things are” and “📁 Documents”, each with an “Open … →” button. On a test copy the first two say “Nothing yet.” Tap “Close”.

steps.do: Tap the card headed “📈 Investments”.
steps.see: A sheet headed “📈 Investments: $539,400”, with a line chart, “🥧 Our mix”, the accounts one by one, and near the bottom “🌤️ Market weather” with a name in big letters. Tap “Close”.

steps.do: Tap the big “📝 Monthly report” button at the bottom of the screen.
steps.see: A sheet headed with last month’s name, starting with a card “🧮 The three answers”, then “📐 Biggest gaps”, “📅 Big-bill savings”, “🚩 Flags” and “📊 Net worth”. Tap “Close”.

steps.do: Tap “⚙️ Settings”, then tap “Monthly income: list each source and its amount.” Change the Pension amount from 5400 to the number below, and tap “Save”. Then tap “Close”.
steps.see: Back on the main screen, the Income row in the three-part card says $9,300.

steps.do: Reload the page (pull it down, or tap ↻ in Safari).
steps.see: The Income row still says $9,300.
steps.tip: If a “What would you like to do?” card comes up, tap “This month” — that is the start menu, and it is right.

steps.do: Turn on Airplane Mode. Tap “✏️ Our budget”, tap the ＋ next to Groceries, and tap “Save the budget” at the bottom.
steps.see: A message says “Budget saved.” — it works with no internet. Now turn Airplane Mode off.

steps.do: Scroll to the top and tap “Set up our own” in the yellow card, then tap OK.
steps.see: A small box first asks “Put the example family away and set up your own?”. After OK, a sheet headed “Before the questions” asks “Are your bank and card statements already saved?” with a “Not yet — just ask me the questions” choice.

steps.do: Tap “Not yet — just ask me the questions”. On question 1, tap “Me and my spouse”, type the words below into the names box, and tap “Next”. On question 2, tap “Done for now”.
steps.see: The main screen shows a card “Question 2 of 19 · Your answers so far are saved.” with a “Carry on with setup” button. The bottom of the page says “Family Money Dashboard v1.3 · 2026-11-14”. Two steps left.

steps.do: Now the videos. This app has 3. Open each one and watch it right through, sound on: Explain it to me — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=familydash&mode=firsttime  Watch it work — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=familydash  Train me — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=familydash&mode=train
steps.see: Each one talks without stopping — no long silences, no sentence starting again. The screen behind the words changes to show what the voice is talking about, and a pointer lands on the thing it names. If the voice talks about a button that is not on the screen, that is a real fault — say which video and which sentence.

steps.do: Last, the shop page everyone sees: https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/ — find Family Money Dashboard on the “Your household” shelf and read its card.
steps.see: The name and the one-line description match the app you just used. The card says Coming soon, and that is right: it joins the store when it passes testing. Nothing on the card promises something the app does not do. If the card and the app disagree, the card is the fault — say which bit.
